problem.title: ForkJoinPool Common Pool Exhaustion via Parallel Stream Blocking I/O
problem.prompt: Batch report generator utilizing Java parallelStreams() to execute external HTTP REST queries.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "The JVM ForkJoinPool.commonPool is reserved strictly for non-blocking in-memory computation; isolate I/O in custom pools."

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Parallel streams run on the shared JVM-wide ForkJoinPool.commonPool() by default (sized to Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors()). Blocking HTTP calls seize all common pool threads, paralyzing unrelated CPU parallel operations across the entire application.
Breakdown Chain: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
